comments.text_zh: 我们的政府没有动力留住他们。他们的主要收入来源不是中小型/创新企业的税收——而是石油和其他自然资源。而开采石油并不需要高等教育和人才。实际上，你根本不需要任何人口。在我看来，他们真正的动机是把高等教育体系关掉，因为 a) 它费钱，b) 它把相当一部分培养出来的人才送到别的国家去，c) 它培养出受过教育的公民，而这些人更难被操纵。遗憾的是，我从在教育行业工作的朋友那里听到了不少印证这一点的说法。顺便说一句，这里有个很棒的视频《Rules for Rulers》，基本上就是《The Dictator's Handbook》的视频版 TL;DR，讲的是民主统治者和专制统治者的动机：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Our government has no incentive to retain them. Their main source of money is not small / medium / innovative business taxation - it's oil and other natural resources. And you don't need higher education and talent to extract oil. Actually, you don't need any population at all. As I see it, their real incentive would be to shut down the higher education system, because it a) costs money, b) sends a good part of produced talent to other countries, and c) produces educated citizens which are harder to manipulate. Sadly, I hear quite a few confirmations of this from friends who work in education. BTW, here's a great video, Rules for Rulers, which is basically a video TL;DR of "The Dictator's Handbook" that explains incentives of democratic and autocratic rulers: [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh:
你说的大部分都对，但我认为你推出的结论是错的。是的，他们确实能抵御因民众情绪变化而产生的摇摆。然而，对于民选官员自己改变主意或改变策略，这就不成立了。他们可能在某个时候承诺某事，然后并不去做。美国历史上充满了被背弃的承诺。一个反例是，Trump 和 Obama 都是直接当选的，尤其在外交关系上，他们拥有巨大权力，想怎么做就怎么做。Obama 承诺了一些东西，Trump 又撤回了。

> 相比之下，独裁政权是不可靠的，因为所有决定都由一个人做出，他的情绪波动会导致大量不可预测性。

理论上这是对的，但实践中许多独裁政权稳定得惊人。独裁者必须讨好他的亲信，他不能想干什么就干什么。他可以在不触及亲信利益的前提下为所欲为。可以查一下政治学里的“Selectorate theory”（选择人理论）。或者看这个很不错的小视频：[VIDEO]
comments.text: You are correct for the most part, but I think you are drawing the wrong implications. Yes, they are resistant to swings based on mood changes in the population. However, this does not hold for changes of mind or strategy by elected people themselves. They might promise something at some point and then not do it. US history is full of broken promises. A counterpoint is that Trump and Obama are elected directly and specially on foreign relations they have a huge power to do whatever they like. Obama promised some stuff, Trump retracted it. > In contrast, a dictatorship is unreliable, because all decisions are made by one person, whose mood swings can result in lots of unpredictability. That is true in theory but in practice many dictatorships are remarkably stable. A dictator has to please his cronies, he can't do whatever he likes. He can do what he likes as long as it does not touch the interest of the cronies. Check "Selectorate theory" in political science. Or this nice little video: [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 我读过《独裁者手册》这本书（想看个好的总结，可以去看 CGP Grey 的视频 Rules for Rulers[1]），我能为这项技术想象出好几个非常清晰且有说服力的 Job Stories：* 作为一个面临大规模抗议的统治者，我想把人群从街上清走，而不必部署那些可能选择站到抗议者一边的士兵。* 作为一个害怕政变的统治者，我想降低维持军队的人事管理成本，这样我就能在保持同等武力致命性的情况下减少所需军官数量。这会让我可以清洗军官团中可能不忠的成员，并重赏留下的人。* 作为一个来自少数族裔/少数宗教群体的统治者，我想把军队成员限制在该少数群体内，同时不降低其致命性，这样我就能防止多数群体成员拥有受过训练的、可能夺取权力或抵抗边缘化的人。像奎宁以及 Madsen 和 Maxim Gun 这样的技术进步，曾让比利时国王 Leopold 手下不到 1,000 名欧洲人[2]把文明的益处[3]传播到刚果——那片面积超过得克萨斯州 3 倍的地方。我很期待这些新进步将带来的世界。[1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK] [3] [LINK]（不过是的，也还有 [LINK]）
comments.text: I've read the book The Dictators Handbook (watch the CGP Grey video Rules for Rulers[1] for a good summary) and I can imagine a number of really clear and compelling Job Stories for this technology: * As a ruler facing large-scale protests, I want to clear the crowds of people from the streets without deploying soldiers who might choose to actually side with the protestors. * As a ruler who is afraid of a coup, I want to reduce the personnel-management costs of maintaining my military so that I can reduce the number of officers needed to maintain the same level of force lethality. This will let me purge my officer corps of possibly-disloyal members and lavish rewards on those who remain. * As a ruler from an ethnic/religious minority, I want to restrict membership in the military to that minority without reducing its lethality so that I can prevent members of the majority from having trained members who could seize power or resist marginalization. Technological advances like quinine and the Madsen and Maxim Gun allowed fewer than 1,000 Europeans[2] under Belgian King Leopold to spread the benefits[3] of civilization to The Congo, an area more than 3 times the size of Texas. I am excited to see the world that these new advances will usher in. [1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK] [3] [LINK] (although yes, also [LINK] )

comments.text_zh: 这篇文章是一个有意思的案例研究，探讨“君主制”与“独裁制”之间的区别。我的理解是，差异如下：* 在君主制下，一个人是“随机”被选中来统治的。在独裁制下，则有一场竞争，最冷酷无情的人得以统治。* 在君主制下，人们相信君主靠君权神授统治。在独裁制下，独裁者靠恐惧统治。* 君主制更稳定，意味着统治者可以做长远规划。独裁者更可能趁还能捞的时候就大肆攫取资源，因为他们害怕政变。* 由于缺乏民意合法性，独裁者被迫考虑下属的自身利益和忠诚。这导致掠夺性和倒退性的政策。看这个解释博弈论的精彩视频：[VIDEO] * 在君主制下，批评受到控制，同时维持法治，靠的是“冒犯君主罪”法律，使批评君主成为非法。在独裁制下，批评靠镇压来控制。而同样的镇压让独裁者更不受欢迎，从而引发更多批评，进而更多镇压，形成恶性循环。君主制是不完美的制度。很大程度上取决于那个被“随机”选中统治的人。但我确实在想，在民主长期失灵、民众教育水平低的国家——比如海地？——君主制是否应该被当作一个选项。大多数成功的民主国家在某个阶段都曾是君主制
comments.text: This article is an interesting case study in the difference between "monarchy" and "dictatorship". The way I think about it, the differences are as follows: * Under monarchy, one person is chosen to rule "at random". Under dictatorship, there is a competition where the most ruthless person gets to rule. * Under monarchy, the people believe the monarch rules by divine right. Under dictatorship, the dictator rules by fear. * Monarchies are more stable, meaning the ruler can plan with a long time horizon. Dictators are more likely to siphon resources while the siphoning is good, since they fear a coup. * Lacking popular legitimacy, a dictator is forced to consider the self-interest and loyalty of their underlings. This leads to extractive and regressive policy. See this excellent video explaining the game theory: [VIDEO] * Under monarchy, criticism is kept in check while maintaining rule of law, via lèse-majesté laws which make it illegal to criticize the monarch. Under dictatorship, criticism is kept in check via repression. That same repression makes the dictator less popular, which triggers more criticism, and thus more repression, in a doom loop. Monarchy is an imperfect system. A lot comes down to the person who is "randomly" chosen to rule. But I do wonder if monarchy should be considered an option in countries where democracy has been consistently dysfunctional and the population is poorly educated -- Haiti perhaps? Most successful democracies were monarchies at some poin

I have doubts that this happened regularly in the past, usually wealthy/powerful were allowed to be toppled by their enemies. I don't know the details of how Weinstein got toppled after so many years of being protected, but my gut says that the people who were protecting him no longer felt like it was worth it to continue. comments.story_title: SBF scheduled to testify tomorrow at US House hearing on FTX collapse
comments.text_zh: 我不认为需要加 /s，“权力”或“权威”的去中心化从来就没成功过。是的，它大概率成功过。只是并非绝对。有一个很强的论点：全部历史都在为这样一种观点提供支持数据——所有社会和政府都处在集权程度上的一条光谱上，而越去中心化的政府对普通人越好。[VIDEO]
comments.text: I don't think the /s is needed, decentralization of "power" or "authority" has never worked. Yes it most likely has. It's just not absolute . There's a very strong argument that all of history is supporting data for all societies and governments being on a spectrum of centralized power, with the more decentralized ones being better for the common person.
